articles.title: Application to Union territories
articles.s: This Part applies to Union Territories, with the President empowered to direct exceptions and modifications; Delhi is exempted.

articles.title: Part not to apply to certain areas
articles.s: This Part does not apply to Scheduled Areas and tribal areas in certain north-eastern states, nor to specified hill areas of Manipur; Parliament may extend Panchayat provisions to Scheduled Areas (done by PESA, 1996).

articles.title: Continuance of existing laws and Panchayats
articles.s: Pre-73rd Amendment Panchayat laws continue for one year unless repealed; existing Panchayats continued till their term's end.

articles.title: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
articles.s: Courts cannot question Panchayat elections except by an election petition presented as the state legislature provides.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.s: Defines 'Committee', 'district', 'Metropolitan area', 'Municipal area', 'Municipality', 'panchayat' and 'population' for this Part (74th Amendment 1992).

articles.title: Constitution of Municipalities
articles.s: There shall be a Nagar Panchayat for transitional areas, a Municipal Council for smaller urban areas, and a Municipal Corporation for larger urban areas in every state.

articles.title: Composition of Municipalities
articles.s: All municipal seats are filled by direct election; the chairperson is elected as the state legislature provides; persons with special knowledge may be represented without voting rights.

articles.title: Constitution and composition of Wards Committees, etc.
articles.s: Wards Committees are constituted for municipalities with 3 lakh or more population, with members chosen from the ward's elected councillors.

articles.title: Reservation of seats
articles.s: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to population, with at least one-third reserved for women (including within SC/ST quotas).

articles.title: Duration of Municipalities, etc.
articles.s: A municipality's term is five years; elections must precede its expiry; a dissolved municipality's fresh election must be held within six months, serving only the remainder of the term.

articles.title: Disqualifications for membership
articles.s: A person is disqualified from municipal membership if disqualified under any law for the state legislature's election, or under any state law; minimum age 21.

articles.title: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities, etc.
articles.s: State legislatures may endow municipalities with powers to function as institutions of self-government, including plans for economic development and social justice and schemes in the Twelfth Schedule's 18 subjects.

articles.title: Power to impose taxes by, and Funds of, the Municipalities
articles.s: State legislatures may authorise municipalities to levy and collect taxes, assign state revenues, and provide for grants-in-aid and Municipal Funds.

articles.title: Finance Commission
articles.s: The State Finance Commission constituted under Article 243-I also reviews municipalities' finances and recommends revenue distribution.

articles.title: Audit of accounts of Municipalities
articles.s: State legislatures may provide for maintenance and audit of municipal accounts.

articles.title: Elections to the Municipalities
articles.s: Municipal elections are conducted under the superintendence, direction and control of the State Election Commission.

articles.title: Application to Union territories
articles.s: This Part applies to Union Territories, with the President empowered to direct exceptions and modifications.

articles.title: Part not to apply to certain areas
articles.s: This Part does not apply to Scheduled Areas and tribal areas under Article 244(1) and (2).

articles.title: Committee for district planning
articles.s: A District Planning Committee consolidates plans prepared by Panchayats and municipalities in each district.

articles.title: Committee for Metropolitan planning
articles.s: A Metropolitan Planning Committee prepares draft development plans for each metropolitan area (population of 10 lakh or more).

articles.title: Continuance of existing laws and Municipalities
articles.s: Pre-74th Amendment municipal laws continue for one year unless repealed; existing municipalities continued till their term's end.

articles.title: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
articles.s: Courts cannot question municipal elections except by an election petition presented as the state legislature provides.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.s: Defines 'authorised person', 'board', 'co-operative society', 'multi-State co-operative society', 'officer', 'Registrar', 'State Act' and 'State level co-operative society' for this Part (97th Amendment 2011).

articles.title: Incorporation of co-operative societies
articles.s: State legislatures make laws for incorporation, regulation and winding up of co-operative societies based on voluntary formation, democratic member-control and professional management. Note: in Rajendra Shah (2013) the Supreme Court struck down Part IXB's application to state co-operative societies for lack of state ratification; the 2021 ruling upheld it only for multi-state co-operative societies.

articles.title: Number and term of members of board and its office bearers
articles.s: A co-operative society's board has up to 21 directors with a five-year term; co-opted members and functional directors are provided for.

articles.title: Election of members of board
articles.s: Board elections are conducted before the term's expiry under the superintendence of an authority designated by the state government.

articles.title: Supersession and suspension of board and interim management
articles.s: A board may be superseded or kept under suspension only in specified situations (persistent default, negligence, etc.) and for a limited period.

articles.title: Audit of accounts of co-operative societies
articles.s: Co-operative societies must get their accounts audited by auditors from a state-approved panel; audit reports go to the general body.

articles.title: Convening of general body meetings
articles.s: The society's annual general body meeting must be convened within six months of the financial year's close.

articles.title: Right of a member to get information
articles.s: Members have the right to access the society's books, information and accounts relating to transactions with them.

articles.title: Returns
articles.s: Every co-operative society files annual returns to the Registrar within six months of the financial year's close.

articles.title: Offences and penalties
articles.s: State legislatures prescribe offences and penalties relating to co-operative societies (false returns, disobedience of Registrar's orders, etc.).

articles.title: Application to multi-State co-operative societies
articles.s: This Part applies to multi-State co-operative societies with Parliament as the competent legislature (upheld for multi-state societies in the Supreme Court's 2021 ruling).

articles.title: Application to Union territories
articles.s: This Part applies to Union Territories with the President empowered to direct exceptions and modifications.

articles.title: Continuance of existing laws
articles.s: Pre-97th Amendment co-operative society laws continue for one year unless repealed or amended.

articles.title: Administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas
articles.s: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are administered under the Fifth Schedule; the tribal areas of those four states under the Sixth Schedule.

articles.title: Formation of an autonomous State comprising certain tribal areas in Assam and creation of local Legislature or Council of Ministers or both therefor
articles.s: Parliament may by law form an autonomous state within Assam comprising specified tribal areas, with its own legislature or Council of Ministers (22nd Amendment 1969; used for Meghalaya's creation).

articles.title: Extent of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States
articles.s: Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of India; a state legislature only for its state (or part of it); no Parliamentary law is invalid merely for extra-territorial operation.
articles.detail: It defines the territorial extent of laws made by Parliament and state legislatures.

articles.title: Subject-matter of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States
articles.s: Distributes legislative subjects via the Seventh Schedule: Parliament over the Union List, states over the State List, both over the Concurrent List; Parliament alone over residuary subjects (Entry 97, Union List).
articles.detail: It distributes legislative subjects between the Union and the States through the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule.

articles.title: Special provision with respect to goods and services tax
articles.s: Both Parliament and state legislatures may make laws on GST: Parliament on inter-state supply (IGST) and states on intra-state supply (SGST/CGST); inserted by the 101st Amendment 2016.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to provide for the establishment of certain additional courts
articles.s: Parliament may establish additional courts for better administration of its laws and matters in the Union List.

articles.title: Residuary powers of legislation
articles.s: Parliament has exclusive power over subjects not enumerated in the State or Concurrent Lists, including taxes not mentioned in either list.
articles.detail: It gives Parliament exclusive power to legislate on residuary subjects, that is, subjects not listed in any of the three lists.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to legislate with respect to a matter in the State List in the national interest
articles.s: Parliament may legislate on a State List subject if the Rajya Sabha resolves by two-thirds of members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest; the resolution lasts one year, renewable.
articles.detail: It allows the Rajya Sabha, by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, to authorise Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to legislate with respect to any matter in the State List if a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation
articles.s: During a National Emergency, Parliament may legislate on any State List subject; such laws cease six months after the Emergency ends.
articles.detail: It gives Parliament the power to legislate on State List subjects while a national emergency is in operation.

articles.title: Inconsistency between laws made by Parliament under articles 249 and 250 and laws made by the Legislatures of States
articles.s: A state law repugnant to a Parliamentary law made under Articles 249 or 250 prevails only so long as the Parliamentary law is in force.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to legislate for two or more States by consent and adoption of such legislation by any other State
articles.s: If two or more states' legislatures resolve that Parliament should regulate a State List matter, Parliament may do so and other states may adopt it (used for the Urban Land Ceiling Act, 1976).
articles.detail: It allows Parliament to legislate for two or more states if those states pass resolutions requesting it.

articles.title: Legislation for giving effect to international agreements
articles.s: Parliament may make laws for implementing treaties and international agreements even on State List subjects (the basis of environmental and trade legislation).
articles.detail: It gives Parliament the power to make laws for implementing international treaties and agreements.

articles.title: Inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and laws made by the Legislatures of States
articles.s: On Concurrent List subjects, a Parliamentary law prevails over a repugnant state law; a state law reserved for and assented to by the President prevails in that state unless Parliament later overrides it (the doctrine of repugnancy).

articles.title: Requirements as to recommendations and previous sanctions to be regarded as matters of procedure only
articles.s: Want of prior recommendation or sanction is a procedural matter: an Act is not invalid merely because assent was given without it, unless the provision itself required it.

articles.title: Obligation of States and the Union
articles.s: State executive power must ensure compliance with Parliamentary laws; the Union's executive power extends to giving directions to states for that purpose.
articles.detail: It obliges states to exercise their executive power so as to ensure compliance with Parliament's laws.

articles.title: Control of the Union over States in certain cases
articles.s: The Union may give directions to states on the construction and maintenance of means of communication of national or military importance and on protection of railways; the extra cost is borne by the Union.
articles.detail: It gives the Union control over states in certain cases, such as the construction and maintenance of means of communication of national importance.

articles.title: Assistance to States by deployment of armed forces or other forces of the Union
articles.s: Let the Union deploy armed or other forces in a state to deal with a grave law-and-order situation; inserted by the 42nd Amendment 1976 and repealed by the 44th Amendment 1978.

articles.title: Power of the Union to confer powers, etc., on States in certain cases
articles.s: The President, with a state's Governor's consent, may entrust Union executive functions to the state government or its officers.

articles.title: Power of the States to entrust functions to the Union
articles.s: A state's Governor, with the President's consent, may entrust state executive functions to the Union government or its officers (42nd Amendment 1976).

articles.title: Armed Forces in States in Part B of the First Schedule
articles.s: Dealt with armed forces in Part B states; omitted by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Jurisdiction of the Union in relation to territories outside India
articles.s: The Union government may exercise jurisdiction in foreign territory by treaty, agreement, grant, usage, sufferance or other lawful means.

articles.title: Public acts, records and judicial proceedings
articles.s: Full faith and credit is given throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every state; Parliament regulates their proof and effect.

articles.title: Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys
articles.s: Parliament may provide for adjudication of inter-state river water disputes (Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956); Parliament may also bar the Supreme Court and other courts from such disputes (used for tribunals like the Cauvery tribunal).

articles.title: Provisions with respect to an inter-State Council
articles.s: The President may establish an Inter-State Council to inquire into and advise on inter-state disputes and subjects of common interest; the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation led to its creation in 1990.
articles.detail: It allows the President to establish an Inter-State Council to coordinate between the Union and the states.

articles.title: Interpretation
articles.s: Defines 'Finance Commission' for this Part.

articles.title: Taxes not to be imposed save by authority of law
articles.s: No tax can be levied or collected except by authority of law (the constitutional basis for challenging illegal taxation).

articles.title: Consolidated Funds and public accounts of India and of the States
articles.s: All revenues form the Consolidated Fund of India (or of the state); money is paid out only under appropriation by law; other public moneys go to the Public Account.

articles.title: Contingency Fund
articles.s: Parliament (and state legislatures) may establish a Contingency Fund in the nature of an imprest, placed at the President's (or Governor's) disposal for unforeseen expenditure.
articles.detail: It provides for the Contingency Fund of India, used for unforeseen expenditure with the President's approval.

articles.title: Duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
articles.s: Stamp duties and excise duties on medicinal and toilet preparations are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the states where levied.

articles.title: Service tax levied by Union and collected and appropriated by the Union and the States
articles.s: Gave the Union power over service tax with collection shared with states; omitted by the 101st Amendment 2016 when GST replaced service tax.

articles.title: Taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States
articles.s: Taxes on sale or purchase of goods (other than newspapers) and taxes on consignment of goods in inter-state trade are levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the states.

articles.title: Levy and collection of goods and services tax in course of inter-State trade or commerce
articles.s: IGST on inter-state supply is levied and collected by the Union and apportioned between the Union and states on GST Council recommendations (101st Amendment 2016).

articles.title: Taxes levied and distributed between the Union and the States
articles.s: All Union taxes and duties (except specified exclusions) form the divisible pool shared with states on Finance Commission recommendations; states currently receive 41 percent under the 15th Finance Commission.

articles.title: Surcharge on certain duties and taxes for purposes of the Union
articles.s: Parliament may levy a surcharge on Union duties and taxes (except GST) for Union purposes; surcharge proceeds go wholly to the Union.

articles.title: Taxes which are levied and collected by the Union and may be distributed between the Union and the States
articles.s: Covered Union excise duties shareable with states; omitted by the 101st Amendment 2016 in the GST overhaul.

articles.title: Grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products
articles.s: Provides for grants-in-aid to Assam, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal in lieu of the former jute export duty.

articles.title: Prior recommendation of President required to Bills affecting taxation in which States are interested
articles.s: Bills affecting taxation in which states are interested need the President's prior recommendation.

articles.title: Grants from the Union to certain States
articles.s: Parliament may provide grants-in-aid to states in need of assistance, charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; includes grants for tribal welfare and raising administration in Scheduled Areas.

articles.title: Taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments
articles.s: States (and local bodies) may levy professional tax up to the prescribed ceiling, currently 2,500 rupees per person per year.

articles.title: Savings
articles.s: Taxes, duties, cesses or fees lawfully levied by states or local bodies before the Constitution's commencement continue until Parliament provides otherwise.

articles.title: Agreement with States in Part B of the First Schedule with regard to certain financial matters
articles.s: Dealt with financial agreements with Part B states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Calculation of "net proceeds", etc.
articles.s: Defines how net proceeds of taxes and duties are calculated (gross proceeds minus cost of collection), certified by the CAG whose certificate is final.

articles.title: Goods and Services Tax Council
articles.s: Constitutes the GST Council (Union Finance Minister as chair, state finance ministers as members) to recommend GST rates, exemptions and thresholds; decisions need a three-fourths majority with the Union holding one-third weight (101st Amendment 2016).

articles.title: Finance Commission
articles.s: The President constitutes a Finance Commission every five years (or earlier) to recommend the distribution of tax proceeds between the Union and states and among states, and grants-in-aid; the 16th Finance Commission (Arvind Panagariya) covers 2026-31.
articles.detail: It provides for a Finance Commission every five years to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the states.

articles.title: Recommendations of the Finance Commission
articles.s: The President lays the Finance Commission's recommendations and the action-taken memorandum before each House of Parliament.

articles.title: Expenditure defrayable by the Union or a State out of its revenues
articles.s: The Union or a state may make grants for any public purpose even beyond its legislative competence (used for centrally sponsored schemes).

articles.title: Custody, etc., of Consolidated Funds, Contingency Funds and moneys credited to the public accounts
articles.s: The custody and payment of moneys into and out of these funds is regulated by Parliamentary (or state) law, and by Presidential (or gubernatorial) rules until then.

articles.title: Custody of suitors' deposits and other moneys received by public servants and courts
articles.s: Moneys received by public servants or courts (other than revenues) are paid into the Public Account of India or the state.

articles.title: Exemption of property of the Union from State taxation
articles.s: Union property is exempt from state taxation unless Parliament provides otherwise.

articles.title: Restrictions as to imposition of tax on the sale or purchase of goods
articles.s: Restricts states' power to tax sale or purchase of goods outside the state or in inter-state trade or commerce (scope reshaped by the 101st Amendment's GST provisions).

articles.title: Exemption from taxes on electricity
articles.s: States cannot tax electricity consumed by the Union or sold to it for its consumption, except under pre-Constitution laws or with the President's assent.

articles.title: Exemption from taxation by States in respect of water or electricity in certain cases
articles.s: States cannot tax water or electricity stored, generated or carried by an inter-state river authority without the President's prior sanction.

articles.title: Exemption of property and income of a State from Union taxation
articles.s: State property and income are exempt from Union taxation; Parliament may tax state business operations by law.

articles.title: Adjustment in respect of certain expenses and pensions
articles.s: The Union and states adjust between themselves expenses and pensions relating to transferred functions and pre-Constitution liabilities.

articles.title: Annual payment to certain Devaswom Funds
articles.s: Kerala pays 46.5 lakh rupees annually to the Travancore Devaswom Fund and 13.5 lakh rupees to the Cochin Devaswom Fund, charged on the state's Consolidated Fund (7th Amendment 1956).

articles.title: Privy purse sums of Rulers
articles.s: Guaranteed privy purse payments to former rulers; repealed by the 26th Amendment 1971 which abolished privy purses.

articles.title: Borrowing by the Government of India
articles.s: The Union government may borrow on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within limits fixed by Parliament.

articles.title: Borrowing by States
articles.s: States may borrow on their Consolidated Fund's security within limits fixed by the legislature; a state indebted to the Union needs the Union's consent to borrow further.

articles.title: Succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations in certain cases
articles.s: Union and state governments succeed to the property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations of the Dominion of India and corresponding provinces.

articles.title: Succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations in other cases
articles.s: Property and assets that vested in His Majesty for the Dominion or a province vest in the Union or the corresponding state, with liabilities apportioned.

articles.title: Property accruing by escheat or lapse or as bona vacantia
articles.s: Property accruing by escheat, lapse or as bona vacantia (ownerless property) vests in the state where situated, or in the Union otherwise.

articles.title: Things of value within territorial waters or continental shelf and resources of the exclusive economic zone to vest in the Union
articles.s: All lands, minerals and other things of value in territorial waters, the continental shelf and the exclusive economic zone vest in the Union (basis of offshore oil and mineral rights).

articles.title: Power to carry on trade or business
articles.s: The Union and states may carry on any trade or business, acquire and dispose of property, and make contracts for any purpose.

articles.title: Contracts
articles.s: Government contracts must be expressed to be made by the President (or Governor), executed by authorised persons, and cannot make the President or Governor personally liable.

articles.title: Suits and proceedings
articles.s: The Government of India may sue or be sued as the Union of India, and a state government as the state, in matters arising from this Part's succession and contract provisions.

articles.title: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
articles.s: No person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law; inserted by the 44th Amendment 1978, making property a constitutional legal right rather than a fundamental right.
articles.detail: It provides that no person shall be deprived of property except by authority of law. After the 44th Amendment in 1978, the right to property is a legal right, not a fundamental right.

articles.title: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse
articles.s: Trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India shall be free, subject to the other provisions of this Part (basis of the common-market doctrine in Atiabari and Automobile Transport cases).

articles.title: Power of Parliament to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse
articles.s: Parliament may restrict trade freedom in the public interest.

articles.title: Restrictions on the legislative powers of the Union and of the States with regard to trade and commerce
articles.s: Neither Parliament nor state legislatures may prefer one state over another or discriminate between states in trade and commerce laws, except to deal with scarcity of goods.

articles.title: Restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse among States
articles.s: States may impose reasonable restrictions in the public interest and non-discriminatory taxes on imported goods, but Bills for the former need the President's prior sanction.

articles.title: Saving of existing laws and laws providing for State monopolies
articles.s: Existing laws and laws creating state monopolies are saved from Articles 301 and 303 (amended by the 4th Amendment 1955).

articles.title: Power of certain States in Part B of the First Schedule to impose restrictions on trade and commerce
articles.s: Let Part B states impose trade restrictions; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956 and not in force.

articles.title: Appointment of authority for carrying out the purposes of articles 301 to 304
articles.s: Parliament may appoint an authority to carry out the purposes of Articles 301 to 304 and confer on it necessary powers (no such authority has been appointed).

articles.title: Interpretation
articles.s: Defines 'State' for this Part as including Union Territories (with adaptations for J and K, which no longer applies after the 2019 reorganisation).

articles.title: Recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the Union or a State
articles.s: Parliament (for Union services) and state legislatures (for state services) regulate recruitment and service conditions; until then the President or Governor regulates them by rules.

articles.title: Tenure of office of persons serving the Union or a State
articles.s: Civil servants hold office during the President's or Governor's pleasure, except as expressly provided by the Constitution.

articles.title: Dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in civil capacities under the Union or a State
articles.s: A civil servant cannot be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to the appointing authority, and cannot be dismissed without an inquiry with a reasonable opportunity of being heard (the Article 311(2) safeguard).

articles.title: All-India services
articles.s: If the Rajya Sabha resolves by two-thirds of members present and voting, Parliament may create new All-India Services (IAS, IPS and IFS exist under this Article; the 28th Amendment 1972 extended it to the All-India Judicial Service, not yet created).
articles.detail: It allows the Rajya Sabha, by a two-thirds majority, to create new All-India Services such as the IAS and IPS.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to vary or revoke conditions of service of officers of certain services
articles.s: Empowers Parliament to vary or revoke pre-Constitution service conditions of ICS and other officers (28th Amendment 1972).

articles.title: Transitional provisions
articles.s: Pre-Constitution laws on public services continue until replaced under Article 309.

articles.title: Provision for protection of existing officers of certain services
articles.s: Protected ICS and other pre-Constitution officers' service conditions; repealed by the 28th Amendment 1972.

articles.title: Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States
articles.s: There shall be a Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and a Public Service Commission for each state.
articles.detail: It provides for the Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions for recruitment to public services.

articles.title: Appointment and term of office of members
articles.s: The UPSC Chairman and members are appointed by the President, and state PSC members by the Governor; they hold office for six years or until age 65 (UPSC) or 62 (state PSC).

articles.title: Removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission
articles.s: A PSC member can be removed only by the President on the Supreme Court's report after inquiry, on grounds of misbehaviour; the President may suspend a member pending inquiry.

articles.title: Power to make regulations as to conditions of service of members and staff of the Commission
articles.s: The President (for UPSC) or Governor (for state PSCs) makes regulations on the number of members, their service conditions and staff.

articles.title: Prohibition as to the holding of offices by members of Commission on ceasing to be such members
articles.s: A UPSC Chairman cannot take further government employment; other members face restrictions on future offices to protect the Commission's independence.

articles.title: Functions of Public Service Commissions
articles.s: PSCs conduct examinations for appointments, advise on recruitment methods, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters; consultation with the PSC is required on specified matters.

articles.title: Power to extend functions of Public Service Commissions
articles.s: Parliament or a state legislature may extend a PSC's functions by law.

articles.title: Expenses of Public Service Commissions
articles.s: UPSC expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; state PSC expenses on the state's Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: Reports of Public Service Commissions
articles.s: The UPSC reports annually to the President and state PSCs to the Governor, who lay the reports with action-taken memoranda before the legislature.

articles.title: Administrative tribunals
articles.s: Parliament may establish administrative tribunals for service disputes of Union, state and local government employees (42nd Amendment 1976; the Central Administrative Tribunal was set up under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985).

articles.title: Tribunals for other matters
articles.s: The appropriate legislature may establish tribunals for tax, industrial, land reform, election and other specified disputes (42nd Amendment 1976; tribunal powers were limited by L. Chandra Kumar, 1997).

articles.title: Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission
articles.s: Elections to Parliament, state legislatures, the President and Vice-President are supervised by the Election Commission, headed by the Chief Election Commissioner and other Commissioners (appointed under the CEC Act, 2023).
articles.detail: It vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.

articles.title: No person to be ineligible for inclusion in, or to claim to be included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex
articles.s: One general electoral roll per constituency; no one may be excluded or included in a separate roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.

articles.title: Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States to be on the basis of adult suffrage
articles.s: Elections are on the basis of adult suffrage: every Indian citizen aged 18 or above may vote (voting age lowered from 21 by the 61st Amendment 1988).
articles.detail: It provides that elections to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies are held on the basis of adult suffrage.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to make provision with respect to elections to Legislatures
articles.s: Parliament may make laws on all electoral matters for Parliament and state legislatures (Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951).

articles.title: Power of Legislature of a State to make provision with respect to elections to such Legislature
articles.s: A state legislature may make electoral laws for its own House, subject to Parliamentary law.

articles.title: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
articles.s: The validity of laws on delimitation and seat allotment cannot be questioned in court; elections can be challenged only by an election petition (Article 329(b)).

articles.title: Special provision as to elections to Parliament in the case of Prime Minister and Speaker
articles.s: Shielded the elections of the PM and Speaker from court challenge; inserted by the 39th Amendment 1975 during the Emergency and repealed by the 44th Amendment 1978.

articles.title: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People
articles.s: Seats are reserved in the Lok Sabha for SCs and STs in proportion to their population in each state.

articles.title: Representation of the Anglo-Indian community in the House of the People
articles.s: Let the President nominate up to two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha if the community was under-represented; omitted by the 104th Amendment 2019 with effect from 25 January 2020.

articles.title: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assemblies of the States
articles.s: Seats are reserved in state Assemblies for SCs and STs in proportion to their population.

articles.title: Representation of the Anglo-Indian community in the Legislative Assemblies of the States
articles.s: Let Governors nominate Anglo-Indians to state Assemblies; omitted by the 104th Amendment 2019.

articles.title: Reservation of seats and special representation to cease after certain period
articles.s: The SC/ST reservation provisions (Articles 330 and 332) were originally to cease after ten years but have been extended repeatedly; the 104th Amendment 2019 extended them to 25 January 2030.

articles.title: Claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to services and posts
articles.s: SC/ST claims are considered in appointments to Union and state services consistently with maintaining administrative efficiency.

articles.title: Special provision for Anglo-Indian community in certain services
articles.s: Reserved Anglo-Indian quotas in railway, customs, postal and telegraph services for the first two years, extended to ten years; long expired.

articles.title: Special provision with respect to educational grants for the benefit of Anglo-Indian community
articles.s: Protected Anglo-Indian educational grants for the first three financial years, extendable by ten years; long expired.

articles.title: National Commission for Scheduled Castes
articles.s: Constitutes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes to investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on SC welfare (separated from the combined SC/ST Commission by the 89th Amendment 2003).

articles.title: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
articles.s: Constitutes the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes to investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on ST welfare (89th Amendment 2003).

articles.title: National Commission for Backward Classes
articles.s: Gives constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (102nd Amendment 2018), which investigates and monitors safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes.

articles.title: Control of the Union over the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes
articles.s: The President may direct states on drawing up and executing tribal welfare schemes; a Commission reports on Scheduled Areas and ST administration (the Dhebar Commission was appointed under this Article).

articles.title: Appointment of a Commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes
articles.s: The President may appoint a Commission to investigate backward-class conditions and recommend steps (the Kalelkar Commission 1953 and Mandal Commission 1979 were appointed under this Article).

articles.title: Scheduled Castes
articles.s: The President, after consulting a state's Governor, notifies the castes deemed Scheduled Castes for that state; Parliament alone may include or exclude castes by law.

articles.title: Scheduled Tribes
articles.s: The President, after consulting a state's Governor, notifies the tribes deemed Scheduled Tribes; Parliament alone may include or exclude tribes by law.

articles.title: Socially and educationally backward classes
articles.s: The President notifies the socially and educationally backward classes for each state or Union Territory in consultation with the Governor; Parliament alone may amend the list; states keep power to identify SEBCs for their own purposes (105th Amendment 2021).

articles.title: Official language of the Union
articles.s: Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the Union; the international form of Indian numerals is used for official purposes.
articles.detail: It declares Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union.

articles.title: Commission and Committee of Parliament on official language
articles.s: The President constitutes an Official Language Commission every five years and a Parliamentary Committee examines its recommendations (the first Commission was appointed in 1955).

articles.title: Official language or languages of a State
articles.s: A state legislature may adopt any language in use in the state (or Hindi) as its official language.

articles.title: Official language for communication between one State and another or between a State and the Union
articles.s: The Union's official language is used for inter-state and Union-state communication, unless states agree on Hindi between themselves.

articles.title: Special provision relating to language spoken by a section of the population of a State
articles.s: The President may recognise a language spoken by a substantial section of a state's population for official purposes on their demand.

articles.title: Language to be used in the Supreme Court and in the High Courts and for Acts, Bills, etc.
articles.s: English is used for Supreme Court and High Court proceedings and for authoritative texts of Bills, Acts and orders, until Parliament provides otherwise.

articles.title: Special procedure for enactment of certain laws relating to language
articles.s: Bills on the language of courts and laws need the President's prior sanction and consideration of the Language Commission's recommendations during the first fifteen years.

articles.title: Language to be used in representations for redress of grievances
articles.s: Every person may submit representations for redress of grievances to Union or state authorities in any language used in the Union or the state.

articles.title: Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage
articles.s: States and local authorities must provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to linguistic minority children (7th Amendment 1956).

articles.title: Special Officer for linguistic minorities
articles.s: The President appoints a Special Officer (Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities) to investigate safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President (7th Amendment 1956).

articles.title: Directive for development of the Hindi language
articles.s: It is the Union's duty to promote the spread of Hindi and develop it as a medium of expression of India's composite culture, drawing on Sanskrit and other Indian languages.

articles.title: Proclamation of Emergency
articles.s: The President may proclaim a National Emergency on the ground of war, external aggression or armed rebellion (substituted for 'internal disturbance' by the 44th Amendment 1978), only on the written advice of the Cabinet; it must be approved by both Houses within one month and can continue with six-monthly approvals. Used in 1962, 1971 and 1975.
articles.detail: It provides for the proclamation of a national emergency on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

articles.title: Effect of Proclamation of Emergency
articles.s: During a National Emergency the Union's executive power extends to giving directions to states, and Parliament may legislate on State List subjects.

articles.title: Application of provisions relating to distribution of revenues while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation
articles.s: The President may modify the revenue-distribution provisions (Articles 268 to 279) during a National Emergency.

articles.title: Duty of the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance
articles.s: The Union must protect every state against external aggression and internal disturbance and ensure state governments run per the Constitution (invoked for central intervention debates).

articles.title: Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States
articles.s: The President may impose President's Rule in a state on the Governor's report (or otherwise) if its government cannot run per the Constitution; it needs Parliamentary approval within two months and can last up to three years with approvals; S.R. Bommai (1994) limited its misuse and made it judicially reviewable.
articles.detail: It provides for President's Rule when the constitutional machinery in a state breaks down.

articles.title: Exercise of legislative powers under Proclamation issued under article 356
articles.s: Parliament may confer the state legislature's law-making power on the President during President's Rule, and authorise expenditure from the state's Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: Suspension of provisions of article 19 during emergencies
articles.s: Article 19 freedoms are automatically suspended during a National Emergency on war or external aggression (not on armed rebellion); the 44th Amendment confined this to war and external aggression only.

articles.title: Suspension of the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies
articles.s: The President may suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21, which the 44th Amendment made non-suspendable) during an Emergency.

articles.title: Provisions as to financial emergency
articles.s: The President may proclaim a Financial Emergency if India's financial stability or credit is threatened; it needs Parliamentary approval within two months; Union directions may include salary reductions of government servants and judges. Never proclaimed.
articles.detail: It provides for a financial emergency if the financial stability of India is threatened. It has never been proclaimed.

articles.title: Protection of President and Governors and Rajpramukhs
articles.s: The President and Governors are not answerable to any court for acts done in the exercise of their powers; no criminal proceedings can be instituted against them during their term.

articles.title: Protection of publication of proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures
articles.s: Protects publication of substantially true reports of Parliamentary and legislature proceedings (44th Amendment 1978; the Feroze Gandhi Act's constitutional basis).

articles.title: Disqualification for appointment on remunerative political post
articles.s: A legislator disqualified under the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection) cannot hold a remunerative political post until re-elected or five years pass, whichever is earlier (91st Amendment 2003).

articles.title: Rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States
articles.s: Guaranteed the rights and privileges of former rulers; repealed by the 26th Amendment 1971.

articles.title: Bar to interference by courts in disputes arising out of certain treaties, agreements, etc.
articles.s: Courts cannot decide disputes arising from pre-Constitution treaties, covenants and sanads of former rulers (used in privy purse litigation).

articles.title: Recognition granted to Rulers of Indian States to cease and privy purses to be abolished
articles.s: Ended recognition of former rulers and abolished privy purses (26th Amendment 1971).

articles.title: Special provisions as to major ports and aerodromes
articles.s: Parliament may declare major ports and aerodromes to be under Union control for specified purposes.

articles.title: Effect of failure to comply with, or to give effect to, directions given by the Union
articles.s: A state's failure to comply with Union directions is lawful ground for the President to hold that the state's government cannot run per the Constitution (a trigger for Article 356).

articles.title: Definitions
articles.s: Defines key terms used in the Constitution, such as 'agricultural income', 'estate duty', 'existing law' and 'railway'.

articles.title: Interpretation
articles.s: Applies the General Clauses Act, 1897 to the Constitution's interpretation unless the context otherwise requires.

articles.title: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
articles.s: Parliament may amend the Constitution by special majority (two-thirds of members present and voting, with a majority of total membership); amendments affecting federal provisions need ratification by half the states; the basic structure cannot be amended (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973).
articles.detail: It lays down the procedure for amending the Constitution, through simple majority, special majority, or special majority with ratification by half the states.

articles.title: Temporary power to Parliament to make laws with respect to certain matters in the State List as if they were matters in the Concurrent List
articles.s: Gave Parliament temporary (five-year) power over certain State List trade and commerce matters after commencement; long expired.

articles.title: Temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir
articles.s: Granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir with limited Union jurisdiction. In August 2019 it was substantially abrogated: C.O. 272 applied all constitutional provisions to J and K, and C.O. 273 declared Article 370 inoperative except its interpretation clause; the J and K Reorganisation Act, 2019 then split the state into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The Supreme Court upheld the abrogation in December 2023 (In re: Article 370).

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat
articles.s: The President may provide for separate development boards for Vidarbha, Marathwada, Saurashtra and Kutch, equitable allocation of funds, and technical education and employment opportunities.

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Nagaland
articles.s: Protects Naga customary law, religious and social practices, and land ownership from Parliamentary Acts unless the Assembly resolves otherwise; reserves Assembly seats and the Governor's special responsibility for law and order (13th Amendment 1962).

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Assam
articles.s: The President may provide for a committee of the Assembly comprising members from the tribal areas of Assam (22nd Amendment 1969).

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Manipur
articles.s: The President may provide for a committee of the Assembly comprising members from the hill areas of Manipur, with the Governor's special responsibility for its working (27th Amendment 1971).

articles.title: Special provisions with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh
articles.s: Provides for equitable opportunities in public employment and education through local cadres and the Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal (32nd Amendment 1973); after bifurcation, its application to Telangana was addressed by later orders.

articles.title: Establishment of Central University in Andhra Pradesh
articles.s: Empowered Parliament to establish a Central University in Andhra Pradesh (32nd Amendment 1973; the University of Hyderabad was set up under it).

articles.title: Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim
articles.s: Protects Sikkim's pre-merger laws, reserves Assembly seats for different sections of the population, and gives the Governor special responsibility for peace and social advancement (36th Amendment 1975).

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Mizoram
articles.s: Protects Mizo customary law, religious and social practices, and land ownership from Parliamentary Acts unless the Assembly resolves otherwise (53rd Amendment 1986).

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Arunachal Pradesh
articles.s: Gives the Governor special responsibility for law and order in Arunachal Pradesh (55th Amendment 1986).

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Goa
articles.s: Reserves at least 30 seats in the Goa Assembly (56th Amendment 1986).

articles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Karnataka
articles.s: Provides for a separate development board for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, equitable fund allocation, and reservation in education and public employment for the region's residents (98th Amendment 2012).

articles.title: Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation
articles.s: Pre-Constitution laws continue in force until altered or repealed, subject to adaptation by the President's orders.

articles.title: Power of the President to adapt laws
articles.s: Empowered the President to adapt laws for the 7th Amendment's state reorganisation by order before 1 November 1957.

articles.title: Power of President to make order in respect of persons under preventive detention in certain cases
articles.s: Empowered the President to order continued preventive detention of persons held under pre-Constitution provincial laws; long expired.

articles.title: Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council
articles.s: Transferred Federal Court judges to the Supreme Court and moved pending cases there at commencement.

articles.title: Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject to the provisions of the Constitution
articles.s: All pre-Constitution courts, authorities and officers continued to function subject to the Constitution.

articles.title: Provisions as to Judges of High Courts
articles.s: Deemed pre-Constitution High Court judges to be judges under the Constitution.

articles.title: Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
articles.s: Deemed the pre-Constitution Auditor-General of India to be the CAG under the Constitution.

articles.title: Provisions as to Public Service Commissions
articles.s: Deemed pre-Constitution Public Service Commissions (Federal and provincial) to be the UPSC and state PSCs under the Constitution.

articles.title: Special provision as to duration of Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly
articles.s: Fixed the duration of the then-existing Andhra Pradesh Assembly (7th Amendment 1956); spent.

articles.title: Provisions as to provisional Parliament and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker thereof
articles.s: Provided for the Constituent Assembly to function as the provisional Parliament; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Provision as to President
articles.s: Provided for the first President's election and term; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Council of Ministers
articles.s: Provided for the first Council of Ministers; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Provisions as to provisional Legislatures for States in Part A of the First Schedule
articles.s: Provided for provisional legislatures in Part A states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Provision as to Governors of Provinces
articles.s: Provided for the first Governors; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Council of Ministers of Governors
articles.s: Provided for Governors' first Councils of Ministers; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Provision as to provisional Legislatures in States in Part B of the First Schedule
articles.s: Provided for provisional legislatures in Part B states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Council of Ministers for States in Part B of the First Schedule
articles.s: Provided for Councils of Ministers in Part B states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Special provision as to determination of population for the purposes of certain elections
articles.s: Provided for population determination for early elections; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Provisions as to the filling of casual vacancies in the provisional Parliament and provisional Legislatures of the States
articles.s: Provided for filling casual vacancies in provisional bodies; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Provision as to Bills pending in the Dominion Legislature and in the Legislatures of Provinces and Indian States
articles.s: Provided for pending Bills at commencement; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Money received or raised or expenditure incurred between the commencement of the Constitution and the 31st day of March, 1950
articles.s: Dealt with transitional finances for 1950; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Power of the President to amend the First and Fourth Schedules in certain contingencies
articles.s: Empowered the President to amend the First and Fourth Schedules by order in contingencies; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

articles.title: Power of the President to remove difficulties
articles.s: Empowers the President to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Constitution by order; in force and available for transitional difficulties.

articles.title: Short title
articles.s: This Constitution may be called the Constitution of India.

articles.title: Commencement
articles.s: Articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 came into force on 26 November 1949; the rest of the Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950.

articles.title: Authoritative text in the Hindi language
articles.s: The President causes an authoritative Hindi translation of the Constitution to be published, with the same meaning as the English text (58th Amendment 1987).

articles.title: Repeals
articles.s: Repeals the Indian Independence Act, 1947 and the Government of India Act, 1935, with all enactments amending or supplementing them.

schedules.title: First Schedule - The States and the Union Territories
schedules.s: Lists the 28 states and 8 Union Territories with their territories; amended whenever states are reorganised (most recently for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh in 2019).

schedules.title: Second Schedule - Emoluments and allowances of constitutional functionaries
schedules.s: Sets out salaries, allowances and privileges of the President, Governors, the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, the CJI and SC judges, the CAG and others.

schedules.title: Third Schedule - Forms of Oaths or Affirmations
schedules.s: Gives the oath forms for Union and state ministers, MPs and MLAs, judges, the CAG and candidates for election.

schedules.title: Fourth Schedule - Allocation of seats in the Council of States
schedules.s: Allocates the 238 elected Rajya Sabha seats among the states and Union Territories.

schedules.title: Fifth Schedule - Administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes
schedules.s: Provides for the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, including Tribes Advisory Councils and the Governor's regulation-making power.

schedules.title: Sixth Schedule - Administration of Tribal Areas in certain north-eastern States
schedules.s: Provides for autonomous district councils in the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, with legislative, executive and limited judicial powers over local matters.

schedules.title: Seventh Schedule - Division of legislative powers: Union, State and Concurrent Lists
schedules.s: Distributes subjects between the Union and states: the Union List (about 100 entries: defence, foreign affairs, railways, banking), the State List (about 61 entries: police, public health, agriculture) and the Concurrent List (about 52 entries: education, forests, criminal law).

schedules.title: Eighth Schedule - Languages
schedules.s: Lists the 22 officially recognised languages: Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santhali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu.

schedules.title: Ninth Schedule - Validation of certain Acts and Regulations
schedules.s: Contains central and state laws (mainly land-reform laws) protected from Fundamental Rights challenges by Article 31B; after I.R. Coelho (2007), insertions after 24 April 1973 are open to basic-structure review.

schedules.title: Tenth Schedule - Disqualification on ground of defection
schedules.s: The anti-defection law (52nd Amendment 1985): an MP or MLA is disqualified for voluntarily giving up party membership or voting against the party whip, subject to the Speaker's decision (judicially reviewable after Kihoto Hollohan, 1992).

schedules.title: Eleventh Schedule - Subjects for Panchayats
schedules.s: Lists 29 subjects over which Panchayats may be given powers under Article 243G, including agriculture, land reforms, minor irrigation, animal husbandry, fisheries, rural housing and poverty alleviation.

schedules.title: Twelfth Schedule - Subjects for Municipalities
schedules.s: Lists 18 subjects over which municipalities may be given powers under Article 243W, including urban planning, water supply, public health, fire services, slum improvement and urban poverty alleviation.
